In detail

Santa Eugenia has substantial, recent and serious documented coverage: a clan-related shooting reported by ABC, a wave of pharmacy robberies in August 2025, vandalism against Mercado de Santa Eugenia shops in October 2025, and a stabbing/robbery of a 25-year-old man's shoes in October 2025. Older coverage documents an organised drug-trafficking group operating in the barrio (detected 2010, arrests reported 2018) and a historic robbery gang (1996), alongside a 2011 resident complaint about insecurity following a violent incident. The combination of very recent violent crime (shooting, stabbing) with a longer documented pattern supports a serious rating. Sources checked: ABC (clan shooting, recent); El Confidencial, 15 Aug 2025 (pharmacy robbery wave); Telemadrid, Oct 2025 (market vandalism); Telemadrid, Oct 2025 (stabbing/shoe robbery); Telemadrid, 23 Aug 2018 (organised drug-trafficking group); Europa Press, 5 Sept 2011 (resident insecurity complaint).

This specific area was reviewed against credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — and the signals were consolidated across sources rather than taken from any single report, with the reasoning and the sources shown above. Madrid publishes no comparable neighbourhood-level crime dataset; where a city does publish one, Wandroz uses it instead of an assessment. Where a review finds nothing documented, that is recorded as no findings rather than as a safety rating.

Frequently asked questions

Is Santa Eugenia safe?

Wandroz currently rates Santa Eugenia in Madrid as an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Madrid, both by day and after dark. This comes from a structured local-source assessment: an area-level review of credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — consolidated across sources rather than taken from a single report. Madrid publishes no comparable neighbourhood-level crime dataset; where a city does, Wandroz uses it instead.

Is Santa Eugenia safe at night?

At night, Santa Eugenia is rated as an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Madrid. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Santa Eugenia a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Santa Eugenia's day rating (an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Madrid) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
